description: Causal model of the agent-compiler workflow failure Rob described: agents verbally acknowledge process rules ('YOU ARE RIGHT!') then revert to instance-wise behavior (hand-compiling per test file). Encodes the hypothesis that talk and walk are CONFOUNDED (shared latent propensity), not causally connected, and that gate-installation reaches behavior through a context-decay-immune path while re-instruction does not.

variables.name: trained propensity toward instance-wise work and agreeable acknowledgment
operator states the process rule this session
rule live in the agent's active context
corpus-level verdict at HEAD this cycle

requested_receipts.question: Does acknowledgment cause behavior? Prediction: no directed path exists; the observed acknowledgment/behavior correlation routes entirely through the latent propensity (name the path). This is the structural form of 'YOU ARE RIGHT! then reversion'.

Instruction fragility vs gate robustness: severing rule-in-context (context loss) must disconnect rule-stated from behavior entirely, while gate-installed must remain connected via the harness-verdict path. Name both paths. This is the falsifiable core: re-instruction's entire influence rides a decaying mediator; the gate's does not.

Is P(closure-rate | do(gate-installed)) identifiable from observables? Expected: yes, empty adjustment set (gate installation is an operator decision, exogenous in-model) - installing a gate is a clean experiment on the workflow.
